summary.headline: Standard Engineering Technology posted FY26 total income of INR793 crores (+26.7% YoY) and PAT of INR83 crores (+21%), but Q4 gross margin fell to ~32% from ~39% in Q3.
summary.overview: Management called FY26 the best year in company history, with revenue, profitability, operating cash flow and working capital all improving together. Q4 total income was INR231 crores (+35% YoY), with EBITDA of INR36 crores (15.5% margin) and PAT of INR21 crores (9.1% margin). Q4 EBITDA was pressured by higher metal input prices and deliberate manpower additions ahead of expected FY27 growth. Management guided FY27 growth and margin improvement qualitatively, with no numeric guidance, and disclosed a new INR130 crore greenfield facility on a 36-acre campus, due in two phases in April 2027 and April 2028.

segments.name: Glass-lined equipment
segments.commentary: Management says glass lining is still about 30% of the business and remains one of the most profitable verticals, though its share is shrinking as other lines grow. Shell and tube glass-lined heat exchangers (with GL HAKKO, Japan) have over 200 units in order book, with 100 delivered.

segments.name: C2C Engineering (acquired)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue was INR24 crores, with order book of about INR46-47 crores. FY27 target is INR60 crores, and margins are said to be similar to the group average.

segments.name: Scigenics (acquired)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR20 crores in FY26 (consolidated for only part of the year). Management targets about INR60 crores in FY27, with margins similar to the group.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue roughly doubled in FY26 versus FY25 per management, but the Q4 export share was 5.3% against guidance of 12-13%. Export order book is only about INR30 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue to grow faster than FY26's 25% rate, per management; no numeric target given.
EBITDA margin in FY27 to improve over FY26 (17.4%); management declined to give a number, and said 'figure I can't confirm' on a 16-17% margin.
Working capital days targeted around 170 in FY27 (vs 150 in FY26), with cash conversion expected to improve versus FY26.
Management expects a INR250-300 crore quarterly revenue run rate from FY27 onwards; said 'possible and definitely we are going to do'.
Capex of INR130 crores over two years for the greenfield facility (INR65 crores in FY27 and INR65 crores in FY28), plus INR35-40 crores for modernisation of existing plants.
Heat exchanger full-fledged Indian manufacturing to start July 1, 2026, with capacity of 200 units per month.
Nuclear and oil and gas entry targeted around FY28.
Pre-cast building subsidiary is being set up to serve pharma and chemical clients only.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about INR40 crores; modernisation of existing plants with robotic and automatic welding and polishing machines continues with another INR35-40 crores planned.
Existing plants run at 70-80% utilisation; management says they can handle 60-70% more revenue after modernisation, taking existing capacity to about INR2,000 crores.
Greenfield 36-acre campus: INR130 crores capex, two phases. Phase 1 (50%) due April 1, 2027; phase 2 due April 1, 2028. Adds about INR2,000 crores capacity, for a total of about INR4,000 crores.

Heat exchanger unit: 80% of equipment is built in Japan and 20% in India. About 50 units were made and sold in India in FY26 (per management), with another 50 in order book. Full-scale Indian manufacturing starts July 1, 2026, at 200 units per month capacity.
Pre-cast building capability for production blocks, targeted to finish in about six months; greenfield projects to complete in 12-14 months.
demand_pricing: Order book is about INR1,000 crores, with about INR30 crores from exports and the balance domestic. Execution is expected in about 8-10 months. Management declined to split the order book by segment.
Advances of 10-30% are taken from customers, typically 20-30%.
Management says it is booking raw materials once orders are received because metal prices are volatile. Freight on exports is passed to customers.

Management claimed a global TAM of USD10 billion for one German competitor's product, with USD5 billion revenue, and a heat exchanger TAM of INR2,000 crores in India (USD2 billion globally). Management says it is the only Indian manufacturer of this product.
Export focus is Europe, US and Middle East; some export discussions were delayed by the war. Management said inventory is mainly raw material and WIP for export and project orders.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall from about 39% in Q3 to 32% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher metal prices and manpower hiring ahead of expected FY27 growth. It said FY27 margins would improve, without a number.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the Q4 export share (5.3%) miss the 12-13% guidance given on the Q3 call?
qa_highlights.answer: A client asked to defer some equipment that was nearly ready. Management said the pending orders would be cleared in Q1 FY27, and export revenue had doubled in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR250-300 crore quarterly revenue run rate achievable from FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, 'possible and definitely we are going to do'.

qa_highlights.question: What are C2C and Scigenics targeting for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: C2C FY26 revenue was INR24 crores, with a target of INR60 crores. Scigenics was about INR20 crores in FY26 and is also targeted at about INR60 crores. Margins are similar to the group.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter pre-cast buildings, and does this raise margin risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said clients insist on civil work, and pre-cast buildings cut build time to 12-14 months. It will serve only pharma and chemical clients and says it is not an EPC business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory of INR438 crores and its ageing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all inventory is under 180 days old, with no dead stock, and it expects to clear it over about 10 months. Inventory is high because of expected FY27 growth. The CFO said inventory days fell after netting customer advances.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from metal prices and manpower costs; Q4 gross margin was about 32%, against about 39% in Q3.
Export execution: Q4 export share of 5.3% missed 12-13% guidance, and USD3.5 million of deferred export equipment is now due in Q1 FY27.
Working capital intensity: management targets about 170 days in FY27, with inventory of about INR438 crores and rising receivables.
Greenfield execution timelines (April 2027 and April 2028) and heat exchanger full-scale start on July 1, 2026.
Management said the war is causing delays in some export discussions, and volatile metal costs are affecting the whole industry.
Governance: Ikeda's re-designation to Executive Director and a new Independent Director are subject to AGM approval. Management also said further acquisitions are planned, with no details.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term growth, with the company describing itself as a unique one-stop solution provider. The tone turns evasive and vague on quantified questions: FY27 margin, order book split, export numbers and the heat exchanger revenue potential. Management also repeated its answers on the pre-cast business and the margin question.

adds.what: Greenfield 36-acre campus facility, phase 1 (50% of INR130 crore capex), adds part of ~INR2,000 crore capacity
Heat exchanger full-scale Indian manufacturing, 200 units per month
Existing plant modernisation (robotic welding and polishing), allowing ~60-70% more revenue from existing capacity to ~INR2,000 crore

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth above FY26's 25% with no numeric target, backed by a ~INR1,000 crore order book executing over 8-10 months, Indian heat exchanger manufacturing from July 2026 at 200 units/month, and a INR130 crore greenfield facility live in phases from April 2027 and April 2028; the INR250-300 crore quarterly run-rate is held but unquantified by timeline beyond FY27.
